podcast.body: This song was included in the torture playlist used at Camp Delta, the military prison at Guantanamo Bay in Cuba. Interrogators utilized this music as part of "enhanced interrogation" tactics on prisoners. "The torture playlist there also included March of the Pigs from 9-Inch Nails. We are the champions from Queen, Springsteens born in the USA, Angel of Death from Slayer, Metallica's won, and tracks from Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Written by Freddie Mercury specifically with soccer (football) in mind, this song was released as a double A-side single with "We Will Rock You" from the 1977 album "News of the World." The song has a feeling of defiance and a chorus suitable for chanting. Ken McCloud notes that Freddie Mercury included lines like "I've done my sentence, but committed no crime," which could be interpreted by the gay community as a reference to their experiences, alongside the song's hyper-masculine elements. It quickly became a sports anthem, embraced by teams celebrating victories. "Freddie Mercury wrote, we are the champion specifically with soccer or football, depending on where you're listening to this. In mind, just as Brian May wrote, we will rock you to be a similar anthem."
